metadata.file_name: 205. Pongsophon (2025). Contrastive Modelling of Self-Regulated Inquiry Behaviours Across Nations: Evidence from TIMSS 2023 Earth Science.pdf
metadata.title: Contrastive modelling of self‐regulated inquiry behaviours across nations: Evidence from TIMSS 2023 Earth Science

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses TIMSS 2023 International Database Grade 8 Earth Science process files and the corresponding Earth Science plausible values, restricted to five countries (Chile, the United Arab Emirates, England, Korea, Turkey) and to a final analytic sample of 25,234 students after preprocessing. The manuscript lists sampling/adjustment weights (e.g., TOTWGT and WGTFAC1–WGTFAC3) in the key-variable table, but it does not explicitly state whether these complex survey weights were applied in the contrastive learning, clustering, and cross-national statistical tests. Because the core modeling is contrastive self-supervised representation learning followed by K-means clustering (and UMAP visualization), the paper does not describe a weight-aware estimation strategy; therefore, weighting usage is unclear from the text. Analysts should consult the TIMSS IDB Analyzer documentation and the authors’ analysis code (if available) to confirm whether TOTWGT/WGTFAC* were used when estimating embedding-cluster differences and country-wise tests.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used TIMSS 2023 Grade 8 Earth Science digital process data (BSPM8 process files) and corresponding Earth Science plausible values. Preprocessing extracted 1176 standardized process indicators (screen visit frequency F, first-visit time R, total time on screen S) and applied mean imputation for missing process indicators, then z-standardized features. For contrastive pair construction, achievement quartiles were used only to create proxy extremes: students in the top 25% and bottom 25% of Earth Science achievement were retained as anchors, while the middle 50% were excluded to maximize behavioral contrast; the final analytic sample comprised 25,234 students across Chile, the UAE, England, Korea, and Turkey.

main_findings.dataset_used: TIMSS 2023 Grade 8 Earth Science process data (BSPM8) across Chile, UAE, England, Korea, Turkey
main_findings.target_variable: Strategic vs non-strategic inquiry profile (cluster membership)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Contrastive training: NT-Xent loss plateau ~0.14 by final epoch; clustering separability: K-means silhouette score = 0.85 (k=2); cross-country clustering by country labels: silhouette score = -0.2399; Kruskal-Wallis on embedding norms across countries: H = 2.2673, p = 0.6867. Additional analysis (Earth Science achievement (Plausible Values) difference between clusters): Cluster-level achievement gap: average Earth Science mean plausible value in the higher-achieving cluster is ~150 points higher than the lower-achieving cluster; distributional evidence: higher-achieving cluster shows narrower interquartile range than the lower-achieving cluster (exact PV summary statistics not numerically reported beyond the ~150-point difference).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TIMSS 2023 Grade 8 Earth Science process data, the study leveraged screen visit frequency (F), first-visit time (R), total time on screen (S), and language of assessment to derive a latent strategic vs non-strategic inquiry profile via contrastive representation learning followed by K-means clustering, finding two well-separated clusters (silhouette = 0.85) that align with SRL-interpretable monitoring-oriented vs surface/fast navigation patterns. This indicates that embedding-based process profiling can support adaptive assessment and real-time scaffolding that targets metacognitive regulation behaviors, while the negative country-label separability suggests these behavioral structures generalize across diverse education systems (though the strategic/non-strategic labels were anchored using achievement quartiles, limiting causal interpretation).

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes TIMSS 2023 Grade 8 Earth Science digital process data (BSPM8) from five countries (Chile, UAE, England, Korea, Turkey), extracting 1176 standardized screen-level indicators capturing screen visit frequency (F), first-visit time (R), and total time on screen (S). Missing process indicators were handled with mean imputation and features were z-standardized; students were retained only from the top and bottom 25% of Earth Science achievement to form proxy extremes, excluding the middle 50% to maximize contrast. A SimCLR-style contrastive representation learning model (MLP encoder with a 128-dimensional projection head; NT-Xent loss) produced embeddings that were clustered with K-means (k=2), yielding strong separability (silhouette = 0.85). Cross-national tests showed no systematic differences in embedding norms across countries (Kruskal–Wallis p = 0.6867) and poor country-based clustering (negative silhouette), suggesting generalizable inquiry structures. The higher-achieving cluster showed an average Earth Science mean plausible value about 150 points higher than the lower-achieving cluster, but the strategic/non-strategic profile construction used achievement quartiles as anchors, so results are correlational rather than causal.
